chunks: From him, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan and Fadalah, from Aban, all of them from Muhammad al-Halabi and Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Ubaydullah al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
"There is no objection to al-muzara'ah (sharecropping) with one-third, one-quarter, or one-fifth."

key_terms.الْمُزَارَعَةِ: Sharecropping; an agricultural contract where the owner provides land and the worker provides labor, sharing the harvest.

ai.seo_question: What are the permissible share ratios for muzara'ah in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* confirms the validity of *muzara'ah* (sharecropping) with flexible harvest divisions, reflecting the practical economic needs of early Shia communities. By explicitly listing one-third, one-quarter, and one-fifth, it demonstrates the juristic flexibility (*tawassu'*) in agricultural contracts, provided the shares are clearly defined and agreed upon by both parties. This ruling underscores the permissibility of profit-sharing models in Islamic law, distinguishing them from fixed-rent arrangements.
